We need a retrosynthesis route up to 5 steps, leaves commercially available, total price <= $9999. Need to propose route using templates. We have one template (38653) that seems to break an ether to give a cyclic acetal? Actually template is a cyclization forming a dioxolane? The product is our target; the reactants are two possible precursors (two isomers). Both are not buyable. Need further disconnections.

We need to find a route: maybe start from simpler building blocks: a dihydroxy cyclohexane derivative with side chain unsaturated acids etc.

Our target: a cyclohexane with two hydroxyls (one primary OH side chain?), plus an ether linking to another cyclohexane? Actually structure: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O. Looks like a bicyclic? Actually it's a cyclohexane with an O-alkyl side chain containing conjugated diene and carboxylic acid.

Simplify: core is a cyclohexane with a secondary alcohol (O- attached to side chain) and a methyl. The side chain is an allylic alcohol (C=C(CO)/C) attached via O to the cyclohexane, then further conjugated diene ending with carboxylic acid.

Potential retrosynthesis: disconnection of the ether (O-alkyl) to give cyclohexanol (protected?) and an allylic alcohol (or acid). So we can use Williamson ether synthesis: cyclohexanol + allylic bromide (or tosylate). So we need cyclohexanol precursor (maybe commercially available) and allylic bromide (maybe derived from acid). The allylic bromide could be derived from the acid via reduction to alcohol then bromination.

Let's search for commercially available cyclohexanol derivatives: maybe (R)-cyclohexanol? The target has stereochemistry; we may need chiral building block. Could use (R)-cyclohex-2-en-1-ol? But we need a specific substitution pattern: cyclohexane with methyl at C1, hydroxyl at C2, and O-alkyl at C3? Actually the SMILES: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O

Let's decode: ring 1: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[...])C... So carbon 1 has OH, carbon 2 is CH2? Hard.

Maybe easier: Use template 38653 which forms a cyclic acetal from a linear precursor? The template seems to convert a linear diene diol into a cyclic acetal? Actually the retro template: [C:1]/[CH]=[CH]/[C:4] >> [C:1]-[C@@H]1-O-[C@H]1-[C:4] (i.e., forms a cyclic acetal from a diene). So applying reverse (forward) would open the cyclic acetal to a diene diol. Our target is a cyclic acetal? It has O-bridge? Actually O[C@H]1...O[C@@H]... forms a 1,3-dioxolane? Not exactly.

The template gave two possible precursors: both are linear molecules with a diene and a carboxylic acid? Let's examine one precursor SMILES: C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/[C@@H]2O[C@H]2C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO

That is a linear chain with a terminal CO (alcohol) and internal cyclic? Actually still cyclic.

Maybe we need to further break the cyclic acetal using another template.

Let's try to apply template 38653 again on one of the precursors? But need to see if applicable.

Take precursor1: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/[C@@H]2O[C@H]2C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO". Apply same template? Might break another ether.

Search for templates that break a C-O bond in a cyclic acetal (like O[C@@H]1...O[C@H]1). Use functional_groups_broken: "ether oxygens". Already used. Maybe need a different template that breaks a C-O bond to give diol.

Search for templates that break "aliphatic hydroxyls"? Let's search for functional_groups_broken "aliphatic hydroxyls".
